reading.body:
Flexential Cincinnati is a 43,551 square foot facility in West Chester, Ohio, with 3.8 MW of critical load UPS capacity. At typical enterprise datacenter density of roughly 10 kW per rack, this capacity supports approximately 380 racks, though this operator publishes no specification of IT load separate from UPS capacity, so that figure is an assumption. The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HIPAA, ISO 27001, SSAE 18, and HITRUST, qualifying it for regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and payment processing.

Within Ohio, Flexential Cincinnati ranks sixth among eight facilities with published megawatt capacity. The state has 76 mapped datacenters overall, but only these eight publish power figures to the operators' spec pages. Ohio's total published capacity is 60.4 MW, making this facility responsible for 6.3 percent of that reported figure.

For AI scaling, 3.8 MW is immaterial at current training cluster scale. High-end AI training densities now run 50 to 150 kW per rack depending on accelerator type, which would reduce the effective rack count to 25 to 75 racks at peak load. This campus serves enterprise and compliance-heavy tenants, not hyperscale compute, and has published no power expansion roadmap.
